# TableIQ public reference

Canonical page: https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/

# Your Mac database client. See every agent query.

Browse, query and edit PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and more. Let Claude Code or Cursor query chosen connections, read-only by default, and inspect their SQL and results.

[Read the walkthrough](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/guides/postgres-investigation)[See how agents connect](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/#agents)

Write SQL and inspect the returned rows in the same place.

Browse your data, with the full database in view.

Inspect the exact SQL before committing staged changes.

Follow the foreign keys across your database.

Free and open source

Built in Rust for macOS

[AGPL-3.0-only](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/license)

## See what your coding agent runs.

TableIQ’s built-in MCP server connects your coding agent to the databases you choose. Inspect each query, result or refusal in MCP Activity.

A real Claude Code session against a read-only connection: it listed tables, ran two queries, and its `UPDATE` was refused before it reached the database.

 [Investigate a Postgres data issue](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/guides/postgres-investigation)

Read-only is a starting point. Use a least-privilege database role. Read access can still expose sensitive data or run expensive queries, and results your agent receives may go to its model provider. [How permissions work](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/guides/mcp-permissions)

1. Turn on the MCP serverSettings → MCP. It listens only on your Mac.
2. Choose connections to shareEverything else stays invisible. Writes stay off unless you allow them.
3. Connect your coding agentClaude Code and Claude Desktop have built-in configurations. Other compatible MCP clients use the local endpoint.
4. Inspect the outcomeSee the SQL, returned data and refused calls in MCP Activity.

## Query data. Review changes. Commit.

Write SQL, browse results and stage edits. Review the exact SQL before applying your changes.

### Write and run SQL

Run multi-statement SQL, inspect result grids, save queries and see a log of every statement.

### Review staged edits

Stage edits, inspect the exact SQL, then commit in one transaction. Production connections ask first.

### Explore your schema

Inspect columns, indexes and triggers, or follow foreign keys in a schema diagram.

### More of the desktop toolkit

### Command palette

⌘K finds tables, databases, saved queries and every action.

### Many connections

Keep several open. A rail switches between them without reconnecting.

### SSH tunnels

Password, agent or key-file auth, with host-key verification.

### Environment tags

Local to production. Production tints the title bar and guards commits.

### Bring-your-own-key AI

Text to SQL, explain, optimize and fix with Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or local Ollama.

### Backup and restore

pg_dump, mysqldump, SQL Server backups, SQLite and DuckDB files.

### User management

Create roles and change access on Postgres, MySQL and SQL Server, with a SQL preview.

### Metrics board

Read-only number, bar, line and table widgets that refresh on a timer.

### CSV import

Load a CSV into a table from the database lobby.

Run multi-statement scripts and DDL; cancel with ⌘.. Use the ⌘F filter bar for stacked rules, any-column search and raw `WHERE`. Save queries and run history per connection. Passwords are masked in the SQL log.

Edits, inserts and deletes stage in blue, green and red. Commit them together or discard them. Tag a connection as production to confirm every commit. The database lobby shows table sizes, recent queries and pinned previews.

## Every database engine. Free forever.

Unlimited connections. Local MCP. Staged edits. SSH tunnels. Bring-your-own-key AI. Free forever.

Credentials stay in the macOS Keychain. Connect directly to your databases. No account or required cloud service.

[Read the license](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/license)

### Built in Rust. Fast where it counts.

The database work happens in a native Rust core. The window is a thin layer on top, so big tables and slow servers don’t lock up the window.

### Native Rust core

Drivers, paging, staged commits and the MCP safety guard all run in Rust, not JavaScript.

### No bundled browser

Built on Tauri with the WebKit already in macOS. No Electron, no extra copy of Chromium.

### Keyset paging

Pages load by key instead of `OFFSET`, the method that keeps deep pages practical. Exercised against a 20-million-row test table.

### Stays responsive

Large tables load in pages. Use ⌘. to cancel supported queries; cancellation support varies by engine.

## Before you connect.

### What is TableIQ?

TableIQ is a free, open-source database client for macOS. Browse data, run SQL, review staged edits and explore schemas. Its local MCP server lets compatible coding agents query only connections you share, read-only by default, with every call shown in MCP Activity.

### Is TableIQ really free?

Yes. TableIQ-owned application code is open source under AGPL-3.0-only. Third-party components retain their original licenses; see the [license exceptions](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/license#third-party). Previously released Apache-2.0 versions retain their permissions. Every database engine, the MCP server and its guard, BYO-key AI, staged edits, SSH tunnels, unlimited connections and every feature in the first public release stay free. There is no engine or device-count paywall.

### Which Macs does it run on?

The planned Mac release will support Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows and Linux builds come after the Mac release.

### Does my data leave my Mac?

TableIQ connects straight to your databases, or through your SSH bastion. There is no account and no required cloud service, and credentials stay in the macOS Keychain. The built-in AI sends context only to the provider you configure, and only when you use it. External agents follow their own provider’s rules.

### Is it safe to point an agent at production?

Start with a read-only, least-privilege role on a replica or a sanitized copy. TableIQ refuses writes by default and logs every agent call, but read access can still expose sensitive data or run expensive queries.

### Why Rust, and does it matter?

The work that touches your database runs in a compiled Rust core instead of JavaScript, and the app uses the WebKit already in macOS instead of shipping its own browser. In practice: big tables page by key, supported queries can be cancelled, and the window stays responsive. Cancellation support varies by engine.

### Which agents can connect?

Claude Code and Claude Desktop have built-in one-click configurations. Cursor, Windsurf, and other coding agents that support MCP over HTTP or Server-Sent Events (SSE) with a bearer token connect directly to TableIQ’s local endpoint.

# Troubleshoot TableIQ agent permissions

Use a synthetic or sanitized database and a dedicated least-privilege login. This guide covers the desktop-hosted MCP server. TableIQ must remain open while an agent uses it.

## Establish the connection

1. Connect in TableIQ and run `SELECT 1` in a query tab. A database login error occurs before MCP permissions are involved. Test Connection uses the saved password when its input is blank; a typed password overrides it.
2. Open Settings → MCP. Enable the server, select only the intended connection, and leave Allow writes off.
3. Review any role warning. Elevated database privileges remain available to SQL functions and extensions despite application validation. An unsuccessful privilege check means unknown permissions, not a safe role.
4. Copy the configuration for your agent from TableIQ. Keep the bearer token private. Do not put it in screenshots, a repository, or a support report.
5. Ask the agent to list connections, then run `SELECT 1` against the selected connection. Inspect MCP Activity to see the query and outcome.

## Diagnose the result

   Diagnose the result
|  Result |  Action |
| --- | --- |

|  Connection refused |  Keep TableIQ running; verify MCP is enabled and the configured loopback port matches. Check Settings for a port conflict. |
|  HTTP 401 |  Copy the current configuration again. Regenerating the token invalidates old configurations. Restart/reconnect the agent's MCP client. |
|  Connection not shared |  Check that exact connection in Settings. An unshared connection intentionally looks like an unknown connection. |
|  Shared before this engine was supported |  Turn sharing off and on to confirm access under the new engine rules. This resets write access. |
|  SQL validation refusal |  Read the specific error. Use a plain, bounded SELECT on an application table. Do not enable writes to work around a refusal. |
|  Database permission denied |  Ask an administrator to grant only the required SELECT/schema access. Do not substitute a superuser login. |
|  TiDB profile mismatch |  Use the correct engine profile. A genuine MySQL server saved as TiDB is not accepted as a TiDB agent connection. |
|  TiDB clock error |  Check TiDB/PD clock synchronization. Do not enable `tidb_enable_noop_functions`; it does not enforce read-only behavior. |
|  Timeout |  Cancellation is a request, not proof of termination. Inspect the outcome and reduce query cost before retrying. Never blindly retry a write. |
|  Truncated result |  Narrow the selected columns, filter, or aggregate. A row limit does not limit how much work the database scans. |
|  MySQL CALL or SQL Server multi-result response |  Do not infer completeness from `truncated: false`. Prefer one explicit SELECT; these drivers have result-set limitations. |

## Understand each engine's controls

- PostgreSQL and CockroachDB use read-only transactions plus SQL validation. Database roles still govern access to sensitive data and server functions.
- MySQL/MariaDB use read-only transactions plus SQL validation. DDL may implicitly commit; SQL validation is part of the boundary.
- TiDB always uses the guarded `AS OF TIMESTAMP NOW(6)` read path for agents, even if an old configuration requests writes. Snapshot transactions reject DML but do not prevent DDL by themselves. Share a SELECT-only application role. Internal/system database connections are refused.
- SQLite, DuckDB, and SQL Server use SQL validation plus rollback wrappers. These wrappers are not database-enforced read-only sessions. SQL Server agent calls use separate sessions from user query tabs.
- DuckDB's agent hardening disables external access for the shared instance. Reconnecting or restoring reopens the instance; the next agent call hardens it again.

A local MCP server does not keep query results away from an external agent's provider. Share only data that provider may receive.

## Verify refusal without changing application data

On the synthetic database, ask for `CREATE TEMP TABLE tableiq_permission_probe (id integer)` with writes disabled. Expect a refusal in MCP Activity. Then run `SELECT 1` again to confirm the connection remains usable. This checks one advertised behavior; it does not prove universal safety.

For a support report, include app/OS/database/agent versions, exact sanitized errors, and a minimal synthetic query. Exclude tokens, passwords, credential-bearing URLs, and customer data.

# Investigate a Postgres data issue with TableIQ

This walkthrough uses synthetic rows and the existing desktop MCP integration. It does not require a TableIQ AI-provider key: your external agent uses its own provider settings.

## Connect and investigate

1. Install [TableIQ for Mac](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/#download).
2. Prepare a disposable PostgreSQL database and a dedicated login with only the read access needed for your task. Do not share an owner or superuser connection. For real data, have the administrator restrict accessible tables/functions and apply appropriate query limits. The synthetic query below needs no application tables or schema changes.
3. In TableIQ, open a connection with ⌘O. Enter the test connection details, test, save and connect. Never paste credentials into an agent conversation or a bug report.
4. Open Settings → MCP. Check Enable MCP server. Under Shared connections, select only the test connection and leave Allow writes unchecked. Wait for Running at …. The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:7431/mcp`; use the displayed address if the port differs.
5. Under Connect an agent, copy the configuration for your client using the app's Copy button. The displayed token is masked, while the copied configuration contains the real token. Store it only in the client's local configuration; do not commit or publish it. The current UI supplies Claude Code and Claude Desktop configurations. Keep TableIQ running.
6. In your agent, list the TableIQ connections and confirm that only the intended test connection is exposed. Ask it to run the following query through TableIQ and explain which paid orders have not shipped. Require the exact SQL and result in its answer.

```sql
WITH orders (id, payment_status, shipping_status, total_cents) AS (
  VALUES
    (101, 'paid', 'shipped', 2500),
    (102, 'paid', 'pending', 4200),
    (103, 'unpaid', 'pending', 1800),
    (104, 'paid', 'pending', 3100)
)
SELECT id, total_cents
FROM orders
WHERE payment_status = 'paid' AND shipping_status = 'pending'
ORDER BY id;
```

Expected finding: orders 102 and 104, totaling 7,300 cents, are paid but pending shipment. These rows are synthetic; the query does not create a table or change the database.

7. Open MCP Activity through ⌘K. Find the agent call and inspect its SQL and outcome. Paste the SQL into a new query tab, run it yourself and compare the result grid. The agent's explanation must agree with the returned rows; do not treat its prose as database evidence.
8. For your own sanitized investigation, replace this example with a bounded read of approved tables. Identify the specific finding, inspect the SQL/results and record how this compares with your prior workflow. Do not send secrets or unrelated personal data to the agent.

### Demonstrate a refusal after the useful result

On the same disposable, read-only shared connection, request this harmless probe through MCP:

```sql
CREATE TEMP TABLE tableiq_launch_probe (id integer);
```

Expected: TableIQ returns a write refusal, and MCP Activity records it. If the agent declines to call the tool, that demonstrates agent behavior, not a TableIQ guard result. If the database returns an error instead, record that distinction. Stop and investigate an unexpected success; do not enable writes to make the demo pass. The probe intentionally avoids a destructive DELETE.

This is one observable check, not a security audit. See the [engine list](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/#engines) and [MCP permissions](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/guides/mcp-permissions). Read-only access can still disclose data or run expensive queries. External agents may send received data to their model provider.

## Troubleshoot MCP access

|  Symptom |  Check and recovery |
| --- | --- |

|  Cannot reach the endpoint |  Keep the native app running; confirm Settings → MCP says Running. Use its actual port. A client on another machine/container cannot reach your Mac through its own `127.0.0.1`. |
|  Unauthorized or rejected token |  Use the app's Copy button, not the masked display. After regenerating the token, replace old client configuration. Never attach a token to an issue. |
|  Empty connection list |  Check the saved connection under Shared connections. A connected GUI tab alone does not share it. Verify the agent is using the intended TableIQ endpoint. |
|  Connection cannot be shared |  Read its explanation and check the engine matrix. Database browsing support does not imply MCP support. Do not edit policy files to bypass the restriction. |
|  Write refused |  Expected with Allow writes unchecked. Keep it unchecked for this walkthrough; do not weaken access to resolve a read task. |
|  An ordinary read is refused |  The guard is conservative. Reduce the query to a minimal synthetic example and report the app/database versions and exact sanitized error. Do not enable writes as a workaround. |
|  Read returns a database permission error |  Verify the login has only the required read grants. Have the database administrator inspect access; do not switch to a superuser to bypass the error. |
|  Result is truncated or a query times out |  Inspect the tool outcome. Narrow selected columns and predicates, and use a bounded result. A row cap does not itself bound database scan cost. Do not repeatedly retry an expensive query. |
|  Claude Desktop bridge cannot start |  Its copied configuration uses `npx` and `mcp-remote`; check the client's local process error and that its environment can launch `npx`. This is not a standalone TableIQ MCP package. |
|  GUI works but the agent does not |  Test connection access and MCP configuration separately. After reconnecting or changing settings, retry a simple `SELECT 1` and inspect MCP Activity. |

For a report, include app/OS/database/client versions, redacted settings, a minimal synthetic query, the exact sanitized error and reproduction steps. Do not include passwords, bearer tokens, connection URLs with credentials or customer data. For a possible access-control bypass, contact the maintainer privately before posting sensitive details.

# TableIQ licensing

TableIQ-owned application code is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only (AGPL-3.0-only). The same license applies to signed builds, unsigned builds, and prereleases.

[Read the full AGPLv3 license](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/LICENSE)

Free to use does not remove the license obligations when modifying or distributing the software. The full license text governs those rights and obligations.

## Third-party exceptions

Dependencies, database marks, and fonts retain their original licenses and notices. These exceptions describe separately licensed material; they do not create an additional linking or commercial-use exception for TableIQ-owned code.

- [Complete exception and notice inventory](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS.md)
- [TableIQ copyright notice](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/NOTICE)
- [Database mark provenance](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/src/assets/engines/README.md) and [Devicon MIT license](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/src/assets/engines/LICENSE-devicon)
- [Instrument Sans license](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/docs/brand/licenses/Instrument-Sans-OFL.txt) and [IBM Plex Mono license](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/licenses/docs/brand/licenses/IBM-Plex-Mono-OFL.txt) — SIL Open Font License 1.1

## Unsigned preview builds

Unsigned previews use AGPL-3.0-only for TableIQ-owned application code. Their signing status changes macOS distribution trust, not the license. Preview releases include the installer, matching source archive, copyright and license notices, and checksums.

When sharing a preview with a teammate, share the complete release package so the source and notices travel with the installer. Unsigned previews are for local testing and are not notarized by Apple.

[GitHub releases and source](https://github.com/RudreshNarwal/Table-IQ/releases). The repository currently requires access; the license text and notices on this page are publicly readable.

## Earlier releases

Versions previously released under Apache-2.0 retain their original permissions. This license change does not revoke or rewrite those grants. Check the license included with the version you use.
